pages.text: The $(item)ADS-B Receiver$() shows the craft its antenna hears on a round green radar screen, north up: range rings, each craft as a block with its track line and a trail of the last half minute, and a tag with its flight ID, altitude in hundreds of feet and speed in knots (^ climbing, v descending).

pages.title: Using it
pages.text: It needs power (4 FE/t) and an $(item)ADS-B Antenna$(): set the antenna on top of it, or coax it from the receiver. How far it hears depends on how high the craft fly, not on the antenna.$(br2)Open it and press On. - and + (or the mouse wheel) set the range, 250 m to 20 km. Click a craft, on the scope or in the list, for its ICAO address, squawk, climb, bearing and distance.

pages.title: Notes
pages.text: While it is on, the square display filling its front shows the live scope in the world too, for anyone within 32 blocks. A receiver on a ship leaves its own ship's beacon off the screen. A craft that stops sending stays as LOST for a few seconds, then goes.$(br2)Cable a $(l:radiocraft:computer/radio_computer)radio computer$(/l) to the receiver (touching, or by $(l:radiocraft:radios/data_wire)data wire$(/l)) to run the $(l:radiocraft:computer/adsb)ADS-B program$(/l) from it.
